name: Coordinate Interval Minor and Product Laws
statement: Signed coordinate symmetries transport $W_i$ with the distinguished coordinate. If a nonempty pc-minor $H$ of $C$ retains $i$, then $W_i(H)\ge W_i(C)$. For nonempty convex-realizable classes on disjoint coordinates, $W_i(C\times F)=W_i(C)$ when $i$ belongs to $C$.
proof: Restricting a realization to the conditioned orthants and projecting preserves every retained-coordinate interval; an exclusive minor word has an exclusive lift. Product projection gives one inequality, while a product realization with a fixed witness in the second factor preserves all intervals and gives the reverse inequality.
